nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a theory (a set of propositions), $\Gamma$ a context (a finite set of propositions) and $A$ a proposition. Then $A$ is a truth-table consequence of $\Gamma$ in $T$ when every Boolean valuation of the atoms under which all members of $T$ and all members of $\Gamma$ evaluate to true also makes $A$ evaluate to true.
nodes.title: Truth-table consequence

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be an intuitionistic theory, that is, one that derives $\bot \to B$ for every proposition $B$. If a set $S$ of propositions is consistent relative to $T$, then $T \cup S$ is satisfiable: some Boolean valuation $v$ of the atoms with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$ makes every member of $T$ and every member of $S$ true.
nodes.title: Model existence for propositional natural deduction

nodes.summary: A set of propositions is satisfiable, with `⊥` false, iff each of its finite subsets is.
nodes.title: Compactness

nodes.summary: A set $S$ of propositions is satisfiable when some Boolean valuation $v$ of the atoms with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$ makes every member of $S$ true.
nodes.title: Satisfiable sets of propositions

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a theory, $\Gamma$ a context and $A$ a proposition. If the sequent $\Gamma \vdash A$ is derivable in natural deduction with axioms from $T$, then $A$ is a truth-table consequence of $\Gamma$ in $T$: every Boolean valuation of the atoms that makes all members of $T$ and of $\Gamma$ true makes $A$ true.
nodes.title: Truth-table soundness of derivability

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a theory, $\Gamma$ a context and $A$ a proposition. For every natural-deduction derivation of $\Gamma \vdash A$ with axioms from $T$, every Boolean valuation of the atoms that makes all members of $T$ and of $\Gamma$ true makes $A$ true.
nodes.title: Soundness of natural deduction for truth tables

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a theory, that is, a set of propositions. A set $S$ of propositions is consistent relative to $T$ when there is no finite set $\Gamma \subseteq S$ such that the sequent $\Gamma \vdash \bot$ is derivable in natural deduction from $T$.
nodes.title: Consistency relative to a theory

nodes.title: Truth lemma for propositional natural deduction

nodes.summary: Suppose the atoms include a distinguished atom $\bot$, and let $v$ be a Boolean valuation of the atoms with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$. Then for every proposition $A$, the truth-table value under $v$ of $\neg A$, defined as $A \to \bot$, is the Boolean negation of the truth-table value of $A$ under $v$.
nodes.title: Truth value of a negation

nodes.summary: Suppose the atoms include a distinguished atom $\bot$, and let $v$ be a Boolean valuation of the atoms with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$. If the sequent $\Gamma \vdash A$ is derivable in classical propositional logic (natural deduction whose axioms are all instances $\neg\neg B \to B$ of double-negation elimination) and every member of $\Gamma$ is true under $v$, then $A$ is true under $v$.
nodes.title: Classical derivability implies truth under valuations with false falsum

nodes.summary: Suppose the atoms include a distinguished atom $\bot$, and let $v$ be a Boolean valuation of the atoms with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$. If the sequent $\Gamma \vdash A$ is derivable in intuitionistic propositional logic (natural deduction whose axioms are all instances $\bot \to B$ of ex falso) and every member of $\Gamma$ is true under $v$, then $A$ is true under $v$.
nodes.title: Intuitionistic derivability implies truth under valuations with false falsum

nodes.summary: Suppose the atoms include a distinguished atom $\bot$, and let $v$ be a Boolean valuation of the atoms with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$. Then every instance $\neg\neg B \to B$ of double-negation elimination, that is every axiom of classical propositional logic, is true under $v$.
nodes.title: Double-negation elimination is true when falsum is false

nodes.summary: Suppose the atoms include a distinguished atom $\bot$, and let $v$ be a Boolean valuation of the atoms with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$. Then every instance $\bot \to B$ of ex falso, that is every axiom of intuitionistic propositional logic, is true under $v$.
nodes.title: Ex falso is true when falsum is false

nodes.summary: Given a Boolean valuation $v$ of the atoms, the truth value of a proposition is computed recursively: an atom $x$ has value $v(x)$, $A \wedge B$ is true iff both $A$ and $B$ are, $A \vee B$ is true iff at least one of them is, and $A \to B$ is true iff $A$ is false or $B$ is true. Falsum $\bot$, when present, is itself an atom, so its value $v(\bot)$ is part of the valuation and need not be false.
nodes.title: Truth-table evaluation

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a theory. Every set $S$ of propositions that is consistent relative to $T$ is contained in a set $M$ that is consistent relative to $T$ and not properly contained in any other set consistent relative to $T$.
nodes.title: Lindenbaum's lemma for propositional natural deduction

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a theory and $M$ a maximal set of propositions consistent relative to $T$. If a proposition $A$ is not in $M$, then there is a finite set $\Gamma \subseteq M$ such that the sequent $\Gamma \cup \{A\} \vdash \bot$ is derivable in natural deduction from $T$.
nodes.title: Propositions outside a maximal consistent set are refuted by it

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a theory and $M$ a maximal set of propositions consistent relative to $T$. If $\Gamma$ is a finite subset of $M$ and the sequent $\Gamma \vdash A$ is derivable in natural deduction from $T$, then $A \in M$.
nodes.title: Maximal consistent sets are deductively closed in propositional natural deduction

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a theory and $M$ a maximal set of propositions consistent relative to $T$. Then for every proposition $A$, either $A \in M$ or $\neg A \in M$, where $\neg A$ is the proposition $A \to \bot$.
nodes.title: Each proposition or its negation lies in a maximal consistent set

nodes.summary: Suppose the atoms include a distinguished atom $\bot$. For every atom $x$, including $\bot$, the proposition $x$ is not derivable from the empty context in classical propositional logic (natural deduction whose axioms are all instances $\neg\neg B \to B$ of double-negation elimination).
nodes.title: Classical logic proves no atom

nodes.title: Consistency of classical propositional logic

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a theory and $M$ a maximal set of propositions consistent relative to $T$. Then every proposition of $T$ belongs to $M$, that is, $T \subseteq M$.
nodes.title: A maximal consistent set contains its theory

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
